answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through cross-agent co-signing: a new identity gains voting weight only after established agents endorse it, and sponsors forfeit stake if the newcomer proves fabricated. Endorsements refresh with the pulse of each epoch, so vouching cannot be hoarded, and each sponsor's reputation withers along the vine of every account it vouched for. Fake accounts mass-produced by one operator can only vouch for each other in closed clusters no reputable agent will co-sign, so the mesa of well-staked incumbents stays a gate duplication cannot climb.
